request_payload.html: Two simpler ways of creating a starter are now possible. One is to use commercial yeast, growing it in flour and water and essentially letting it become wild again; the other is to buy a culture from long established vendor. Specialty and natural food stores often sell them, or you could try looking online. Sourdoughs International (208-382-4828; www.sourdo.com) in Cascade, Idaho, carries starters from around the world. King Arthur Flour (800-827-6836; www. kingarthurflour.com) carries French and New England sourdough starters, and for taste of authentic Oregon Trail sourdough, contact the friends of the late Carl Griffith, an enthusiast who shared his family’s starter throughout his lifetime (http://home.att. net/~carlsfriends;CarlsFriends@att.net).
